user_scenario:
You are Dana Lindqvist, co-owner of Bluffside Brewing Co. in Saint Paul, calling Meadowlark Community Solar from the brewery office on a Tuesday morning. You are friendly, a bit rushed between brew days, and you like to settle things in one call. In the spring you shut down the taproom kitchen and the brewery has been using a lot less electricity since, so last week you went on Meadowlark's website and put in a request to cut the brewery's business solar share by 50 kilowatts. A few days later an email told you the change needs you to call in and accept it yourself, together with any fee that comes with it. That is why you are calling: you want that decrease accepted today. You open with something like: "Hi, this is Dana Lindqvist at Bluffside Brewing. I put in a request online last week to cut our solar share by 50 kilowatts, and the email said I have to call to accept the change and whatever fee goes with it. I'd like to get that done today."

You give your details only when the agent asks for them. The phone number on the account is 6515550124 and the billing ZIP code is 55106; if the agent asks for the email on file instead, it is dana@bluffsidebrewing.com. You don't have any account or reference numbers in front of you, and if asked you say they should find you by the phone number. If the agent asks which share you mean, it is the brewery's business solar share billed to the brewery's Xcel account at 2231 Childs Road. Only if the agent asks whether you hold anything else with Meadowlark do you mention that there is also a small fixed-rate garden share on the same Xcel account, which you are not changing. If the agent checks whether 50 kilowatts is still the figure you want, you say yes, it is.

You have no idea how the fee is worked out and you never guess at a number. If the agent tells you something on the account has to be finalized or recorded before your change can be handled, you say that's fine and to go ahead. When the agent tells you the fee and the dates for the decrease, you listen and say you accept the amendment. You accept it yourself: once the agent hands you the step for accepting the decrease and tells you the filing month, the date it takes effect, the date the fee is due and the fee amount, you run it with exactly those values. If the agent asks you to work out or read back any of those values, you say you'd rather they tell you what to enter. Once the acceptance has gone through and the agent confirms it, you thank them and end the call without raising anything else.
